not useful enough to be profitable

our_interpretation: The context identifies the technology as LLMs. The statement describes present commercial viability and reliability, rather than a forecast.

The ordinary reading of the profitability clause is that selling LLM-based services cannot presently cover their costs. Provider accounts and product accounts can test that assertion, but neither revenue growth nor positive gross margins alone establishes profitability.

For the ongoing financial observation, use April–June 2026, the latest completed calendar quarter that could have been reported before the August 25 post. This reporting-period choice is supplied by the evaluator.

Profitability ordinarily requires accounting for all attributable costs. The speaker does not specify net income, operating income, an accounting basis, particular providers, or whether he means providers or individual products.
World-changing ordinarily suggests broad consequential effects. The wording supplies no measurable scale of impact or reliability threshold.
Provider losses alone cannot establish that insufficient usefulness caused those losses.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable accounts showing that major LLM businesses and representative products could not cover their attributable costs would support the financial clause. Supporting the entire claim would additionally require evidence linking those losses to insufficient usefulness and showing that reliability prevented broadly consequential deployment.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Verified, sustained profitability of an LLM business or product after attributable costs would contradict the blanket commercial assertion. Broad consequential deployment with adequate measured reliability would challenge the reliability clause, although the speaker supplies no threshold for that test.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: Comparable full-cost provider and product accounts for the target period, with a specified profit measure and accounting basis, could settle the commercial clause. The reliability clause additionally requires a defined consequential-impact test and deployment evidence connecting reliability to that test.
